findings.claim: In removeOwnerRules, sameFiles.has relies on os.Stat of the earlier path. When the first file is removed (for example one that install created and uninstall deletes once empty), a later path that is a symlink or case-variant of it no longer resolves, so os.SameFile cannot match. That path is then processed again and can be reported a second time. This is the same-file-once claim not holding for the uninstall case where a file was created by install; it is unproven for the hard-link and dangling cases. The tests only cover a pre-existing shared file.

evidence: The identity check in sameFiles.has is evaluated against the file system at call time. It matches on the cleaned path first, and otherwise on os.SameFile of two successful stats.
The apply.sh indent_lines change is correct for multi-line and empty results; the here-string supplies the final newline.
install and status check after the first write, so a newly created shared file is detected there.
